name: Citation Reliability in AI Writing
title: Citation Reliability in AI Writing
answer: Language models still fabricate references. A 2023 study found 55 percent of citations produced by GPT-3.5 and 18 percent of those produced by GPT-4 were fabricated, and later tests across many models found wide variation, so every reference in AI assisted writing must be checked against the source.

reading.body:
Fabricated citations remain a live risk in AI writing, and the rate varies so widely by model that no reference can be trusted unchecked.

The measured spread is the point. In 2023, 55 percent of GPT-3.5 citations and 18 percent of GPT-4 citations were fabricated. A later preprint put hallucination rates across 13 models anywhere from about 14 to 95 percent. The newer model in the first study fabricated far fewer references than the older one, but the second study shows that improvement did not generalize into a safe floor. A model that fabricates one reference in seven is still unusable for citation work without verification.

For medical writing this is a production constraint, not a caution. A fabricated reference in a regulatory submission or an evidence dossier is a traceability failure, and the fix is architectural: generate citations only from a retrieved document set and verify each one against the source. That means retrieval and checking sit in the pipeline, not in a reviewer's good intentions. It also means the compute spent on grounding and verification is part of the cost of using these models at all, not an optional add-on.

The data covers fabrication rates and the control that follows from them. It does not say which models perform best now, how rates shift with retrieval, or how often fabricated citations survive into published work.

sections.body: Generate citations only from a retrieved document set and verify each one; never accept a reference the model produced from memory.
